_why: Pass one of the Leonardo-buildings pipeline. Goal is NOT a final asset: it is to prove that a Leonardo-generated building can be brought into the castle's register, and to find an angle + framing recipe Raheem can then drive himself in Leonardo. Raheem, 2026-08-07: 'make it look like how the current castle is, but spruced up... imagine this castle, but 4K'.
_model_choice: Phoenix, because it is the ONLY model that accepts the style-reference controlnet (harness.mjs:201 — Lucid Origin and KINO reject it outright). Matching the existing castle is a STRUCTURAL problem, not an adjectival one, so pointing Leonardo at the real castle art beats describing it. The companion config building-forge-lucid.json runs the same brief on Lucid Origin with no reference, as the control.
_alchemy: false on purpose. lib/pixelize.py records the finding: Alchemy ON returns a 3D render, OFF returns a smooth painted render. Neither is pixel art — that is what pixelize.py is for — but OFF is far closer to a flat game asset.
_style_ref: castle-tower-watch-v2.png flattened onto white. Chosen over the wall and gatehouse because it is a COMPLETE free-standing building in the target register, so it teaches palette and framing at once. Flattened because a transparent surround uploads as black and drags the whole palette dark.
_native_scale: The castle kit's own pieces are 288x384 (tower) and 384x288 (wall). Generate large here, then downsample to that register via lib/pixelize.py. Do not chase a final-resolution asset out of Leonardo.

styleHeader: 2D game art asset: a single free-standing fantasy building shown as a clean front elevation with only a slight downward tilt so a little of the rooftop is visible, in the style of a classic 16-bit top-down RPG. Flat cel-shaded rendering with clean dark outlines, a strictly limited palette, and chunky bold readable shapes. Stone is lavender-grey blockwork with darker violet mortar lines and occasional cream accent blocks; all trim, arch stones, banding and roof caps are warm amber gold. The building stands completely alone, centred, on a plain flat solid white background with absolutely no ground, no grass, no paving, no sky, no horizon, no scenery, no cast shadow and no other objects.

familyLabels.forge: The Forge — exterior, castle register (Phoenix + castle style reference)

states.label: A — squat smithy, single great chimney
states.line: A blacksmith's forge building: a squat, sturdy stone smithy roughly as wide as it is tall, with a broad shingled roof and one massive stone chimney stack rising from the left side, warm smoke curling from its top. Set into the centre of the front wall is a DEEP RECESSED ARCHWAY with amber gold voussoir stones around it, and from inside that archway a strong orange furnace glow spills outward. A heavy iron-banded anvil stands on a stone block to the right of the doorway, with a rack of hammers and tongs mounted on the wall beside it. Small arrow-slit windows glow warm from within.

states.label: B — tall forge tower with attached workshop
states.line: A blacksmith's forge building: a tall narrow stone forge tower with amber gold crenellations at its top and a tapering chimney flue venting warm smoke, with a lower single-storey workshop wing attached to its right side under a shingled roof. The workshop wing has a DEEP RECESSED ARCHWAY doorway ringed with amber gold voussoir stones, glowing strongly orange from the furnace within. Barrels and a stone water-quench trough sit against the wall. Narrow arrow-slit windows up the tower glow warm.

states.label: C — wide open-fronted forge hall
states.line: A blacksmith's forge building: a wide, low, open-fronted stone forge hall, considerably wider than it is tall, with a long shingled roof carried on stout stone piers and two chimney stacks venting warm smoke at either end. The centre of the front is a DEEP RECESSED ARCHED opening ringed with amber gold voussoir stones, through which a great orange furnace fire glows. An anvil on a stone block and a rack of finished blades stand under the overhang. Amber gold banding runs along the roofline.
